newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas steady to lower ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas steady to lower ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were unchanged to slightly lower Friday as cooler temperatures moved into the South, thereby eliminating most air-conditioning demand, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices slipped one cent to $1.92-1.97 per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted mostly at $1.96 and $1.97.

In south Texas, prices were similarly lower in the low-$1.90s as forecasters called for temperatures to be about five- to 10-degrees Fahrenheit below normal this weekend in the state and stretching into the southern plains.
In the East, where temperatures are expected to hover about eight to 12 degrees F below seasonable norms this weekend, New York city-gate prices were steady to slightly higher around $2.30.
In the Appalachian region, prices on Columbia drifted to about $2.05-2.10, while prices on CNG were talked at $2.16-2.18.
In the Midcontinent, prices fell by an average of three cents to the high-$1.80s as storage injections slowed ahead of colder temperatures this weekend.

Chicago city-gate values were at $2.00-2.05, also down about three cents from Thursday's levels. At the Detroit city-gate, where ice storms resulted in extensive power outages, gas prices were talked at $2.06-2.08.
Detroit Edison said more than 200,000 of its customers were without service this morning, while CMS Energy's power outages totalled about 142,000, the company said.
In the Permian basin, gas prices eased by about four cents to the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s, while Waha prices were talked at $1.84-1.88.
"We thought it was going to go down substantially, but it never did," one Texas-based trader said, as the heat continued to blanket the Southwest.
Southern California border prices were equally lower at $1.85-1.90.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California is still expected to restart around March 20 following repairs of a leak, Edison International said.
